hypothesis: A broad 50-position quality-momentum sleeve with positive 60-day trend confirmation and 60-day holding can retain positive net alpha under 5x costs while distributing profit across enough names to serve as a third portfolio profit source.
design_disclosure: R339 showed every tested narrow sleeve failed the third-source screen. Rather than forcing a failed 10-position sleeve into the portfolio, R340 creates one new broad sleeve. It is a structural breadth/turnover experiment, not a factor-weight or holding-period grid.

fixed_construction.universe: daily historical HS300 membership, standard R340 strategy basic filters
fixed_construction.entry_filter: ma60 present, momentum_60d > 0, quality/cash/low-vol factors non-null
fixed_construction.score: momentum_60d 40% + quality-value 25% + cash quality 20% + low volatility 15%

screen_gates.D1: strategy loads and required factors are available
screen_gates.D2: 2x and 5x curves cover the full common window
screen_gates.E4: maximum daily-return correlation with existing A and B <=0.85

selection_rule: If all D/E gates pass, this broad sleeve becomes the fixed C sleeve for a separately preregistered three-sleeve portfolio test. If any gate fails, record a negative result and do not alter weights, holding period, TopN or factor definitions after reading results.

future_portfolio_test_if_eligible.structure: A/B/C monthly 60-day inverse-volatility risk parity, each weight [0.20,0.60], equity sleeve max 1/3, unchanged three-asset defensive bucket, 60d/15% overlay, no leverage
future_portfolio_test_if_eligible.promotion_requires: new preregistration and all portfolio performance, cost, concentration, asset-substitution, plateau and fresh-start gates

known_limitations: In-sample post-hoc strategy created after observing concentration failures.
60-day holding is not a grid-selected optimum.
Current industry and financial snapshots are not full vendor PIT reconstructions.
The strategy is not deployable merely because its standalone screen passes.
